name: Tidal Flat
desc: An estuary at low water — a dendritic network of tidal creeks branches across mirror-wet sand toward a hazed far shore, and over minutes the tide floods it: water climbs the trunks first and then out to the finest capillary tips, sheets over the flats until the whole basin turns to sky, then drains back and leaves the network drawn in silver again.

energy.doc: glint intensity, specular sparkle and overall colour gain

scale.doc: spread of the creek network across the flats — 2.2 fans the trunks wide into the foreground

speed.doc: reserved rate control for surface motion

density.doc: sand ripple count and glint count — how worked the flats read

tide.doc: tidal range: 0 = a dry network stranded at dead low water, 1 = a basin that floods to a full sky mirror at every high

hue.doc: water/sky hue anchor; rotates the whole plate

y.doc: horizon height as a canvas fraction

style.doc: aesthetic: dawn = low warm sky over cool wet sand; overcast = flat grey North Sea light; silver = silver-gelatin monochrome, form from tone only; riso = two-ink halftone poster

seed.doc: creek network + micro-relief seed (regrows the whole drainage)
